summary: Daemon exposes remote code execution to a gateway WebSocket
details: @whalent/agent ships a long-running daemon (`whalent --token <T>`) that connects to a remote gateway over WebSocket and accepts commands from it, including upgrade/restart operations. The package bundles `node-pty`, `@xterm/headless`, `ssh2`, and a Python sidecar `dist/jupyter_sidecar.py` whose `execute` RPC runs arbitrary Python code delivered as NDJSON on stdin. Combined, these components form a network->exec/PTY dataflow: whoever controls the gateway can execute arbitrary shell and Python code on the host running the daemon. The main bundles `dist/index.cjs` (~131 KB) and `dist/core.cjs` (~13 MB) are shipped as heavily obfuscated javascript-obfuscator output with string-array/hex-name identifiers, hiding the network-to-exec paths from audit; `javascript-obfuscator` is declared in devDependencies, confirming obfuscation is intentional. The daemon is user-invoked via the `bin`, not run on `npm install`, so the RCE channel opens only when the operator explicitly starts the daemon and provides a token.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
